chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ, from ʿAbdullāh — meaning Ibn Sinān — from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If an elderly man and an elderly woman commit adultery, they are lashed and then stoned as a punishment for them. If a middle-aged man commits adultery, he is stoned and not lashed, if he is muḥṣan. And if a young man commits adultery, he is lashed one hundred times and exiled for one year from his city.

key_terms.أُحْصِنَ: he was muḥṣan, meaning legally protected through marriage
key_terms.مِصْرِهِ: his city or place of residence
key_terms.نُفِيَ سَنَةً: he was exiled for one year

ai.seo_question: What punishment does this hadith prescribe for zina in different cases?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines legal punishments for zina in different cases, distinguishing between the elderly, the middle-aged muḥṣan man, and the young offender. It reflects a fiqh-based classification of hadd penalties and exile in the administration of criminal law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5032 - It is narrated by Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Muhammad ibn Hafs from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:

"If an elderly man and an elderly woman commit adultery, they should first be lashed and then stoned as a punishment for them.
If a middle-aged man commits adultery and he is married (muhṣan), he should be stoned but not lashed.
However, if a young man commits adultery, he should be lashed one hundred times and exiled for one year from his city."
